newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says has Russian offer of guns, planes.
newsitem.headline: Manila says has Russian offer of guns, planes.

text.p: Russia has offered to sell the Philippines fighter jets and guns to help modernise its armed forces, foreign undersecretary Rodolfo Severino said on Monday.
Severino visited Moscow last weekend where he held talks with his Russian deputy foreign minister Trigori Karasin.

He said the Russians offered "all kinds of things, from fighter aircraft to small arms." Philippine officials earlier said they were considering offers froms several countries to help modernise the country's ill-equipped armed forces.
Manila has earmarked $2 billion for the military modernisation programme with spending to be spread over 15 years.
The deadline for the submission of bids for air force equipment was on May 30. Military officials said they expected to make a decision soon.

Armed forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera said recently the Philippines was shopping for 24 second-hand fighter jets and a dozen naval vessels. Among the planes Manila was looking at were U.S.-made F-16s and Russian-made MIG-29s, he said.

Recent disputes between the Philippines and China over ownership of some islands and rocks in the South China Sea have prompted Philippine congressional leaders to urge Manila to speed up the modernisation programme.
"Russia is a Pacific power and we urged them to remain engaged in the region," Severino said.
